title: What is the area of the third diamond inside?
description: A diamond of area sixty four square centimetres has a new diamond drawn inside it by joining the midpoints of its sides, again and again. The video folds the corners in to see the inner shape is half, then halves three times. Keeko's doubt is that each shape is a quarter of the one before.
teaching_notes: One idea: joining the midpoints of the sides keeps exactly half of the area, so the area is halved for each new shape. Watch for students who take a quarter instead of a half.

source: A diamond pattern has area 64 square cm. Each new shape is d
video_script.why: The child has seen diamonds inside diamonds in the blanket of the book and now links the drawing to halving the area.
video_script.substitution: Fold the four corner triangles onto the inner shape to see it is half, then halve the area once for each new shape.
video_script.anchor: the blanket of the book, with diamond shaped patterns inside diamond shaped patterns
video_script.wrong_answer: the third shape is one square centimetre
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko thinks each inner shape is a quarter of the one before and gets one square centimetre. The four corner triangles fold in and cover the inner shape, so each new shape is half, not a quarter.
video_script.payoff_line: The third shape inside has an area of eight square centimetres
maths_rules: joining the midpoints of the sides keeps exactly half: the four corner triangles fold in and cover the inner shape
slip: taking a quarter gives 64 / 4 = 16, 16 / 4 = 4, 4 / 4 = 1, which is wrong
video_script.design: One diamond on the stage with its midpoints joined; the corners fold in; then the nested shapes are shown with their areas written beside them.

beats.on_screen: a small title card From your book; a blanket with a diamond pattern; the outer diamond is labelled 64 square cm; three smaller diamonds sit inside

marks.book: the title card and the blanket appear
marks.area: the outer diamond is labelled with its area

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This is a question from your book about a blanket with diamond shaped patterns.
<bookmark mark='area'/>The outer diamond has an area of sixty four square centimetres.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>Each new diamond joins the midpoints of the sides of the one before. What is the area of the third shape inside?

beats.on_screen: the blanket stays on the board with the third shape outlined

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

beats.on_screen: one diamond alone on the stage; a dot at the middle of each side; the dots are joined to make a shape inside; four corner triangles are shaded

marks.mark: a dot appears at the middle of each side
marks.join: the four dots are joined by lines
marks.corner: the four corner triangles are shaded

narration: <bookmark mark='mark'/>Draw one diamond and mark the midpoint of each side.
<bookmark mark='join'/>Join the midpoints to make a new shape inside.
<bookmark mark='corner'/>The four corner triangles are left outside the new shape.

beats.on_screen: Given: outer diamond 64 square cm. Each new shape joins the midpoints of the sides of the one before.

marks.given: the outer area and the rule are written

narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, the outer diamond has an area of sixty four square centimetres. Each new shape joins the midpoints of the sides of the one before.

beats.on_screen: To find: area of the third shape inside

marks.find: the words third shape inside are written

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find the area of the third shape inside.

beats.on_screen: The 4 corner triangles fold in and cover the inner shape exactly. Inner shape = half of the shape before.

marks.fold: all four corner triangles fold in over the inner shape
marks.half: the label half appears on the inner shape

narration: <bookmark mark='fold'/>Step one, fold the four corner triangles in. They cover the inner shape exactly, with no gap and no overlap.
<bookmark mark='half'/>The corners are as big as the inner shape. The inner shape is half of the shape before.

marks.calc: 64 / 2 = 32 is written beside the first shape inside

narration: <bookmark mark='calc'/>Step two, halve the outer area to get the first shape inside. Sixty four divided by two is thirty two square centimetres.

marks.calc: 32 / 2 = 16 is written beside the second shape inside

narration: <bookmark mark='calc'/>Step three, halve again to get the second shape inside. Thirty two divided by two is sixteen square centimetres.

marks.calc: 16 / 2 = 8 is written beside the third shape inside

narration: <bookmark mark='calc'/>Step four, halve once more to get the third shape inside. Sixteen divided by two is eight square centimetres.
<bookmark mark='ans'/>The third shape inside has an area of eight square centimetres.

beats.on_screen: Keeko with a raised hand beside the nested diamonds
narration: <bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: Keeko's bubble shows 64, 16, 4, 1, struck through; the four corner triangles fold in again over the inner shape

marks.fold: the four corner triangles fold in again over the inner shape
marks.fix: the bubble is struck through and the label half returns

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks each inner shape is a quarter of the one before. Then the third shape is one square centimetre.
<bookmark mark='fold'/>Fold the four corners in again. They cover the inner shape with no gap left.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>A quarter is too small. Each new shape is half of the one before.
